establish an integrated, statewide rural healthcare workforce pipeline through Alabama’s community colleges. The system will expand rural healthcare training capacity at Alabama’s community college, enabling students to earn healthcare job credentials without relocating. The project will establish remote emergency medical technician (EMT) and advanced EMT tracks. It also will expand allied health training through a centralized pipeline using shared curriculum, procurement and support across rural community colleges in respiratory therapy, surgical technology, radiologic technology, medical lab technology and medication technician program. It will increase nursing capacity through additional faculty, simulation resources, instructional sites and new paths to nursing education. The program also will establish a structured rural pipeline to advanced nursing careers, including nurse practitioner, physician assistant and certified nurse midwife (Statewide).
